solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Right to hold spoon, say, close to chin

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

blocks.note: to spoon is to lie snugly together, so spooning is one way to lie
the last letter of chin

explanation.surface: A diner holds a spoon up near the chin, perhaps feeding a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to hold' is the definition, not an instruction to put letters inside others; 'say' marks spooning as an example of lying.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim entitling a creditor to retain another's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Opening couplet from Lovelace certainly ready for respect

indicators.note: a couplet is a pair, so the opening two letters of the following name are taken

blocks.note: the first two letters of Lovelace
OK, an informal yes
up to, as in up to the job

explanation.surface: A reader admires the first two lines of a poem by the Cavalier poet Richard Lovelace.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up to someone is an idiom for admiring and respecting them.

clue.text: I struggle with sums? Uni and me aren't suitably disposed

definitions.note: a self-description standing for an adjective

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so these letters are set out in a suitable new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A student admits that they and their university are not well suited to maths.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a speaker describing themselves: someone who says 'I struggle with sums' is innumerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Innumerate is the numerical counterpart of illiterate: lacking basic arithmetic skill.

clue.text: Women diving into Seine, racily modern stuff

indicators.note: something diving into water ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other
done racily, in a lively or loose way, these letters lose their original order

blocks.note: the river's name taken as written
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Parisian women plunging into the Seine, a daring new fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Newies is an informal plural noun for new things, novelties or recent productions.

clue.text: Kids' cave with ordinary opening

blocks.note: cave (Latin for beware) is school slang for a warning cry, as golfers shout fore
W is the abbreviation for with
ord. is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: Children have a cave with a plain, ordinary entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cave is not a hollow in rock but the schoolboy warning, pronounced KAY-vee; the golfer's fore is a cry of the same kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreword is the introductory section opening a book, written before the main text.

clue.text: Fine once due on a trading transport group

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a lot is a share or levy owed, as in scot and lot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A penalty payment is owed on a shipping consortium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as historical: a flota sailed long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The flota was the Spanish treasure fleet that once carried trade goods between Spain and its American colonies.

clue.text: Old Mexican's some cool mechanic

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is used

blocks.note: spans the end of cool and the start of mechanic

explanation.surface: An ancient Mexican turns out to be a rather cool car mechanic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olmec were an early Mesoamerican civilisation on the Gulf coast of Mexico, so one of them is an ancient Mexican.

clue.text: I respond as head of Jewish seminary accepting answer

definitions.note: a self-description standing for a noun

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece is received inside the other

blocks.note: a rector heads a college or seminary; Chambers names a Jesuit seminary
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: The principal of a religious college replies to a question.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers defines a rector as head of a Jesuit seminary; the blog transcription, and so this clue, reads Jewish, which the blogger acknowledged as a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is one who reacts, so it can speak of itself as one that responds.

clue.text: Nimble for some is short of colour, Carol goes without second

indicators.note: going without something means losing it, here the word's second letter

blocks.note: wan means pale, lacking colour
a noel is a Christmas carol

explanation.surface: An agile figure looks pale while a carol is sung without a second voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some' marks the definition as dialect: wannel is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, wannel describes a body that is supple and agile, so it is a regional word for nimble.

clue.text: Unpleasant film goes cravenly over slaughter

blocks.note: to oil in slang is to flatter or creep, behaving in a servile way
to lick is to thrash or beat soundly

explanation.surface: A nasty movie fawningly glosses over a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places one piece above the other in this down clue. 'Film' suggests cinema but is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil slick is a thin, polluting layer of oil spread over water, literally an unpleasant film.

clue.text: Old salt's not entirely old secret

indicators.note: not the entire word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: dearn is an archaic word for secret; the old before it flags the word as archaic

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor keeps only part of a long-held secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old salt' suggests a sailor, but salt is a dated slang adjective meaning costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is old slang for expensive, and dear also means high-priced.

clue.text: Oddly winsome fille I labelled falsely European

indicators.note: falsely suggests misrepresented, so these letters are put out of their true order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly tagged a charming young French girl as European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' belongs to the definition, not an alternate-letter signal; fille is French for girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle laide is a woman whose plain or unconventional features nonetheless make her attractive, a strangely appealing girl.

clue.text: Subject to moan we revised individual's job description

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: on, as in on condition of
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whose complaint has been edited sees their job role revised.
explanation.definitionFit: One-woman describes a show or business run by a single person, so it describes an individual's work.

clue.text: Grit and audacity in a style of some axemen?

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Courage and nerve displayed by a team of woodcutters.
explanation.walkthrough: Axemen suggests woodcutters, but an axe is slang for a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottleneck is a slide guitar technique, played with a glass neck on the finger, so it is a guitarists' style.

clue.text: Fighting aircraft accommodating upper-class male

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: kite is slang for an aircraft
U is the abbreviation for upper-class
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A combat plane carries a posh man on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Kumite is free sparring in karate, the fighting part of training.

clue.text: Who finds fault with being held by coroner?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun

indicators.note: something held by another sits within its grasp, so it goes inside

blocks.note: cor. is the abbreviation for coroner
ens is the philosophical term for being or existence

explanation.surface: A question asking who criticises things when a coroner is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor, in an older sense, is a critic: one who censures or passes judgement on faults.

clue.text: Sustain deal involving piffle that's central to Boris

indicators.note: involving means enclosing or including, so the following parts go within
what is central to a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: a pact is an agreement
rot means nonsense
the middle letter of Boris

explanation.surface: A political pact full of nonsense typical of Boris Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or draw out, keeping something going longer.

clue.text: Punt is stuffed by learner's sloshes

indicators.note: something stuffed has a filling put into it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a punt is a wager
L is the learner-driver plate
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A trainee punter rows a flat-bottomed boat and splashes water about.
explanation.walkthrough: Punt and sloshes suggest boats and water; sloshes is slang for hits.
explanation.definitionFit: To slosh someone is slang for hitting them hard, and to belt is likewise to strike.

clue.text: Brand adopting King Edward's support structure

indicators.note: to adopt is to take into the family, so one piece is taken inside

blocks.note: a stigma is a brand or mark of disgrace
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A potato brand takes on King Edward, the variety, as a supporting product.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is also a familiar British potato variety, which steers the surface toward vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A sterigma is a small stalk in fungi that bears and holds up a spore, a botanical supporting structure.

clue.text: Cordial Middle Easterner and Crown Office cancelling article

indicators.note: to cancel is to strike out, so a word is removed from the rest

blocks.note: a Persian is from Iran
CO is the abbreviation for Crown Office
an is the indefinite article, the piece removed

explanation.surface: A friendly Iranian and a government department have scrapped a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like the adjective friendly but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Persico is a liqueur flavoured with peach or apricot kernels, a sweet cordial.

clue.text: Canadian cooked a fungus

blocks.note: Can. is the abbreviation for Canadian
to do food is to cook it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Canadian chef prepared a mushroom dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like an anagram signal, but there are not enough letters; it gives a whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Candida is a genus of yeast-like fungi, including the one that causes thrush.

clue.text: Old light burning in fort

indicators.note: in places one part within the other here

blocks.note: Ft is the abbreviation for fort
lit means alight

explanation.surface: An ancient lamp still glows inside a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' suggests a lamp, but here it is the adjective meaning nimble or quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Flitt is an obsolete Spenserian word meaning fleet or swift, light on one's feet.

clue.text: Scots coup it to be highly wicked

blocks.note: 't is the clipped form of it, as in 'tis
wicked is slang for excellent, and to rock is to be excellent

explanation.surface: A Scottish coup d'etat considered thoroughly evil.
explanation.walkthrough: Coup is not an overthrow but a Scots verb meaning to barter, and wicked is the slang term of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Trock is a Scots verb meaning to barter or exchange, which is also a Scots sense of coup.

clue.text: Company about to pawn digger?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
to hock something is to pawn it

explanation.surface: A firm is about to sell off its excavator at a pawnshop.
explanation.walkthrough: Digger is Australian slang for a soldier; the question mark signals that a chocko is a kind of digger.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocko is Australian slang for a militiaman or conscript, a chocolate soldier, so a kind of Australian soldier.

clue.text: Say, a suffix lacking power

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a particle in grammar can be a prefix or suffix
P is the abbreviation for power, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A grammar note offering an example of a suffix missing some force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks an example: the word 'a' is one instance of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'a' is the indefinite article, so it is an example of the grammatical category.

clue.text: Even elements in firm ridicule being mischievous

indicators.note: the even elements are the letters in second and fourth places

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of firm
pish is an exclamation of contempt; to pish is to scorn

explanation.surface: Mocking rivals within a company is just playful mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish means behaving like an imp, playfully naughty.

clue.text: Old hat's spoiled. Damn and blast!

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so these letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone swears on finding an old hat ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Damn and blast are curses, and curses are oaths in the sense of profane swearing.

clue.text: Staff money used in subverting ideal glamour

indicators.note: something used in a mixture is put inside it
to subvert is literally to turn from below, so in a down entry the order is turned upside down

blocks.note: a halo is an aura of glory or idealised glamour
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Employees' pay is being spent on undermining a glamorous ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Omlah is an Anglo-Indian word for the body of officials in a court or office, a staff.

clue.text: Lag must accept length on one's bird

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the following pieces go inside

blocks.note: an old lag is a convict
L is the abbreviation for length
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prisoner has to admit to doing a long stretch of bird, prison time.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is slang for a prison sentence, which fits the lag in the surface, but here it is a real bird. 'on' sets length before one.
explanation.definitionFit: The colin is the North American bobwhite quail, a game bird.

clue.text: Terrible Tudor's town

indicators.note: terrible suggests damaged or wrecked, so these letters are put into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A town belonging to a dreadful Tudor monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: STROUD is a market town in Gloucestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroud is a town in the Cotswolds in western England.

clue.text: With last two off support, eg, Juliet's stage direction alone

indicators.note: with the last two letters taken off, the end of the word is cut

blocks.note: solace is comfort and support

explanation.surface: An actress playing Juliet gets a stage instruction to be alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Sola is the feminine form, used for a female character such as Juliet; a male one would be solus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sola is the Latin stage direction telling a female character that she is alone on stage.

clue.text: Tree within part of Tibetan temple circling pole

indicators.note: within places one piece inside another
circling round turns a word to face the other way

blocks.note: a mani is a stone prayer wall in a Tibetan Buddhist temple
PO is the abbreviation for pole

explanation.surface: A tree grows inside part of a Tibetan temple, encircling a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The mopani is a southern African hardwood tree with butterfly-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Take up, please, a kilt

blocks.note: to fill is to take up space
I beg is a polite request

explanation.surface: A request to shorten a kilt by taking up its hem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take up' suggests hemming a garment but means occupy.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibeg is the Highland kilt, a pleated knee-length skirt.

clue.text: Want a sarcastic term of esteem that's out of use, alas!

blocks.note: to want is to lack
taken as written

blocks.clueFragment: sarcastic term of esteem that's out of use
blocks.note: a daisy was dated slang for something first-rate, often used ironically

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that an old ironic compliment has fallen out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackadaisy is an archaic exclamation of sorrow, a variant of lackaday, so it means alas.

clue.text: Where Fahrer drives about freely? Nah, recklessly

indicators.note: freely means without constraint, so these letters move into a new order
done recklessly, wildly, so these letters too are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German driver speeds about at will, dismissing caution.
explanation.walkthrough: Fahrer is German for driver.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, where German drivers famously drive fast.

clue.text: I'm avoiding physician before pre-match performance

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping it out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to remove
a hakim is a Muslim physician
a. is the abbreviation for ante, Latin for before

explanation.surface: A sportsman skips the doctor's check before the team's pre-game ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is the Maori war dance performed by New Zealand rugby teams before matches.
